essay.en:
Surah ad-Dukhan opens with an oath: God swears by the Manifest Book that He sent it down on a blessed night, warning mankind, for on that night every definitive matter is resolved as an ordinance from Him. Al-Tabatabai reads the whole surah as a warning to those who doubt this Book, holding over them the threat of punishment in this world and the next [1]. The blessed night is the Night of Ordainment; some read it as mid-Sha'ban, but Tabrisi and Tusi hold the first sounder, since the Quran came down in Ramadan [3][6]. Shia tafsir adds that what is decreed that night passes from the Prophet to Ali and the Imams, down to the Master of the Age [12].

The Book is a mercy from the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the one God who gives life and brings death. Yet the doubters only play in their doubt, so the Prophet is told to watch for the day the sky brings on a manifest smoke that envelops the people. They will cry that it is a painful punishment and beg for relief, promising to believe; but the reminder will not avail them, for a manifest apostle had already come and they turned away, calling him a tutored madman. Commentators dispute what the smoke is [2].

To steady the Prophet, God then recalls the people of Pharaoh. A noble apostle, Moses, came asking them to give over the servants of God and not to defy Him; they threatened to stone him, and he took refuge in his Lord. Pharaoh's host pursued Israel through the sea, left unmoving behind them, and was drowned. They abandoned gardens, springs and splendid places, bequeathed to another people, and neither the sky nor the earth wept for them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: سَأَلَ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَم) عَنْ قَوْلِ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِنَّا أَنْزَلْناهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ قَالَ نَعَمْ لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ وَهِيَ فِي كُلِّ سَنَةٍ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فِي الْعَشْرِ الأَوَاخِرِ فَلَمْ يُنْزَلِ الْقُرْآنُ إِلاَّ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ قَالَ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِيها يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ قَالَ يُقَدَّرُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ كُلُّ شَيْ‏ءٍ يَكُونُ فِي تِلْكَ السَّنَةِ إِلَى مِثْلِهَا مِنْ قَابِلٍ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from al-Fudayl, Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Humran

text.en: Humran asked Abu Jafar about God's words, 'We sent it down on a blessed night.' He said: Yes, it is the Night of Ordainment, which comes every year in the last ten days of Ramadan; the Quran was sent down only on the Night of Ordainment. On it everything of the coming year is measured out.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Kazim
narrations.arabic: أما حم فهو محمد … و أما الكتاب المبين فهو أمير المؤمنين علي … و أما الليلة ففاطمة … يقول: يخرج منها خير كثير، فرجل حكيم، و رجل حكيم، و رجل حكيم
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ahmad ibn Mihran and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Yaqub ibn Jafar

text.en: As for Ha, Meem, it is Muhammad. As for the Manifest Book, it is the Commander of the Faithful, Ali. As for the night, it is Fatimah. And 'on it every definitive matter is resolved' means much good comes forth from her: a man of wisdom, a man of wisdom, and a man of wisdom.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: قَالَ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ فِيها يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ يَقُولُ يَنْزِلُ فِيهَا كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ … إِنَّهُ لَيَنْزِلُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ إِلَى وَلِيِّ الامْرِ تَفْسِيرُ الامُورِ سَنَةً سَنَةً يُؤْمَرُ فِيهَا فِي أَمْرِ نَفْسِهِ بِكَذَا وَكَذَا وَفِي أَمْرِ النَّاسِ بِكَذَا وَكَذَا

text.en: God says of the Night of Ordainment, 'On it every definitive matter is resolved' - meaning every wise matter is sent down on it. On the Night of Ordainment the explanation of affairs descends, year by year, to the one who holds God's command; he is instructed on it about his own affair and the people's affair.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إِذَا كَانَ لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ فِيها يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ نَادَى مُنَادٍ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ مِنْ بُطْنَانِ الْعَرْشِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ غَفَرَ لِمَنْ زَارَ قَبْرَ الْحُسَيْنِ (ع) فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ
narrations.chain: by his chain, from Sandal, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When it is the Night of Ordainment, on which every definitive matter is resolved, a herald calls out that night from the depths of the Throne: God has forgiven whoever visited the grave of Husayn on this night.

narrations.speaker: Amir al-Muminin
narrations.arabic: مر عليه رجل عدو لله ولرسوله، فقال: { وما بكت عليهم السماء والأرض وما كانوا منظرين } ثم مر عليه الحسين بن علي عليهما السلام فقال: لكن هذا ليبكين عليه السماء والأرض، وقال: وما بكت السماء والأرض إلا على يحيى بن زكريا والحسين بن علي عليهما السلام
narrations.chain: his father, from Hannan ibn Sadir, from Abdullah ibn al-Fudayl al-Hamdani, from his father, from his grandfather, from Amir al-Muminin

text.en: An enemy of God and His Messenger passed by him, and he recited, 'Neither the sky wept for them, nor the earth.' Then Husayn ibn Ali passed by, and he said: But for this one the sky and earth will surely weep - they have wept for none but Yahya ibn Zakariyya and Husayn.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: بكت السماء على يحيى بن زكريا، و على الحسين بن علي (عليهم السلام)، أربعين صباحا، و لم تبك إلا عليهما، قلت: فما بكاؤها؟ قال: كانت تطلع حمراء و تغيب حمراء
narrations.chain: al-Tabrisi, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The sky wept for Yahya ibn Zakariyya and for Husayn ibn Ali forty mornings, and it wept for none but them. When asked how it wept, he said: It would rise red and set red.

perspectives.en: Commentators split over the smoke of verse 10. The prevailing Sunni reading, which al-Tabari adopts from Ibn Masud, is that the smoke was the famine that struck Mecca after the Prophet prayed against Quraysh, a distress they saw between themselves and the sky and which is now long past [34]. Shia tafsir preserves a different reading: al-Qummi ties the smoke to the Raj'a, the return from the graves that is still to come [14]. Both traditions also record the view that the smoke is a portent of the Hour yet to appear.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: يتلخص غرض السورة في إنذار المرتابين في الكتاب بعذاب الدنيا وعذاب الآخرة

sources.gloss: The purpose of the surah comes down to warning those who doubt the Book with the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: واختلف في المراد بهذا العذاب المذكور في الآية

sources.gloss: They differed over what is meant by this punishment mentioned in the verse.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: الليلة المباركة هي ليلة القدر … وقيل هي ليلة النصف من شعبان عن عكرمة والأصحّ الأول

sources.gloss: The blessed night is the Night of Ordainment; and it is said to be the night of mid-Sha'ban, from Ikrimah, but the first is sounder.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وهي ليلة القدر … وقال قوم: هي ليلة النصف من شعبان. والأول أصح

sources.gloss: It is the Night of Ordainment; and some said it is the night of mid-Sha'ban, but the first is sounder.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: ويلقيه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله إلى أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام ويلقيه أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام إلى الأئمة عليهم السلام حتى ينتهي ذلك إلى صاحب الزمان عليه السلام

sources.gloss: The Messenger of God conveys it to the Commander of the Faithful, and the Commander of the Faithful conveys it to the Imams, until it reaches the Master of the Age.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: { يوم تأتي السماء بدخان مبين } قال: ذلك إذا خرجوا في الرجعة من القبر

sources.gloss: 'The day the sky brings on a manifest smoke' - he said: that is when they come out in the Return from the grave.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وما بكت السماء والأرض إلا على يحيى بن زكريا والحسين بن علي عليهما السلام

sources.gloss: The sky and the earth wept for none but Yahya ibn Zakariyya and Husayn ibn Ali.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أما حم فهو محمد … و أما الكتاب المبين فهو أمير المؤمنين علي … و أما الليلة ففاطمة

sources.gloss: As for Ha, Meem, it is Muhammad; as for the Manifest Book, it is the Commander of the Faithful, Ali; as for the night, it is Fatimah.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: بكت السماء على يحيى بن زكريا، و على الحسين بن علي (عليهم السلام)، أربعين صباحا، و لم تبك إلا عليهما

sources.gloss: The sky wept for Yahya ibn Zakariyya and for Husayn ibn Ali forty mornings, and it wept for none but them.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: وأولى القولين بالصواب في ذلك ما رُوي عن ابن مسعود من أن الدخان الذي أمر الله نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يرتقبه، هو ما أصاب قومه من الجهد بدعائه عليهم

sources.gloss: The sounder of the two views is what is related from Ibn Masud, that the smoke which God ordered His Prophet to await was the distress that befell his people through his supplication against them.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: نَعَمْ لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ وَهِيَ فِي كُلِّ سَنَةٍ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فِي الْعَشْرِ الأَوَاخِرِ

sources.gloss: Yes, it is the Night of Ordainment, which falls every year in the last ten days of the month of Ramadan.

sources.author: shaykh jafar b. muhammad al-qummi

excerpt.text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ غَفَرَ لِمَنْ زَارَ قَبْرَ الْحُسَيْنِ (ع) فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ

sources.gloss: God has forgiven whoever has visited the grave of Husayn on this night.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: إِنَّهُ لَيَنْزِلُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ إِلَى وَلِيِّ الامْرِ تَفْسِيرُ الامُورِ سَنَةً سَنَةً

sources.gloss: On the Night of Ordainment, the explanation of affairs descends, year by year, to the one who holds God's command.

title.en: Deliverance and the denial of resurrection

essay.en:
This passage closes the account of Moses and Pharaoh that the surah had been telling [1]. Allah recalls that He delivered the Children of Israel from Pharaoh's humiliating torment - the slaying of their sons and the enslaving of their women - and that Pharaoh was a tyrant who overstepped every bound [3]. He chose them knowingly above the nations, which the commentators read as the nations of their own time, favoured through the Torah and the prophets raised among them [3][5], and He gave them signs that held a manifest test, whether by blessing or by hardship [3]. Al-Mizan hears in this ending a reassurance to the Prophet that Allah will likewise deliver him and the believers from the Pharaohs of Quraysh [1].

The address then turns back to the Meccans, who deny the resurrection - it will be only our first death, they say, and we shall not be resurrected, so bring our fathers back if you are truthful [2][5]. The Quran does not take up the taunt but warns them - are they mightier than the people of Tubba and the nations before them, whom Allah destroyed for their guilt [2][6]? Then it sets out the proof they overlook: the heavens and the earth were not created for play, but only with truth, and most people do not know it [2][6]. A creation that merely raised things up and let them perish would be idle, and because Allah does not act in vain, a lasting world must follow [6].

That world has its fixed day, the Day of Judgement, the appointed time that gathers them all [2][3]. On it no friend can avail a friend and none are helped [4]; the worldly ties that once availed have fallen away [2]. The one exception is the person on whom Allah has mercy. The commentators leave room here for the intercession that comes only by Allah's leave [4][7], while the narrations identify the excepted ones as Ali and his followers [13]. It seals the warning with His two names: He is the All-mighty, the All-merciful [2].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: الأئمة من المؤمنين، و فضلناهم على من سواهم
narrations.chain: From one who related it, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Concerning His words, 'Certainly We chose them knowingly above all the nations': they are the Imams from among the believers, and We favoured them over all others.

note.en: Tubba was a title of the kings of Yemen; the commentators identify this one as a Himyarite king and report that he himself had accepted faith, so the verse blames his people and not him [3].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إنّ تبّعاً قال للأوس والخزرج كونوا ها هنا حتى يخرج هذا النبي أما أنا لو أدركته لخدمته وخرجت معه
narrations.chain: Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Tubba said to the Aws and the Khazraj, 'Stay here until this Prophet comes forth. As for me, had I lived to reach him, I would have served him and gone out with him.'

note.en: The commentators read this as denying any helper who could act without Allah's leave, so it leaves room for the intercession He permits [4].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: نَحْنُ وَالله الَّذِي رَحِمَ الله وَنَحْنُ وَالله الَّذِي اسْتَثْنَى الله لَكِنَّا نُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Abd al-Azim al-Hasani, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Zayd al-Shahham

text.en: We, by Allah, are those on whom Allah has mercy; and we, by Allah, are those whom Allah excepted; yet we shall avail them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ما استثنى الله عز ذكره بأحد من أوصياء الأنبياء و لا أتباعهم ما خلا أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام) و شيعته … يعني بذلك عليا (عليه السلام) و شيعته
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: O Abu Muhammad, Allah made an exception for none of the successors of the prophets or their followers save Amir al-Mu'minin and his shia; He means by that Ali and his shia.

perspectives.en: Verse 42's exception, 'except for him on whom Allah has mercy,' is read differently. The Sunni commentators apply it to the believers at large: al-Tabari takes the excepted one as the person interceded for before his Lord [20], and Ibn Kathir says nothing avails on that day but Allah's mercy on His creation [23]. The Shia narrations read it more precisely - those whom Allah excepted are Ali and his followers [13] - a reading al-Mizan places among the Quran's proofs of intercession [2]. Both traditions thus leave the door open to intercession by Allah's leave.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: نوع تطييب لنفس النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وإيماء إلى أن الله تعالى سينجّيه والمؤمنين به من فراعنة مكة ويختارهم ويمكنهم في الأرض

sources.gloss: a comfort to the Prophet and a hint that Allah will deliver him and the believers from the Pharaohs of Mecca, and will choose them and establish them in the land.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: والآية من أدلة الشفاعة يومئذ

sources.gloss: and this verse is among the proofs of intercession on that day.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: اخترنا موسى وقومه بني إسرائيل وفضّلناهم بالتوراة وكثرة الأنبياء منهم

sources.gloss: We chose Moses and his people, the Children of Israel, and favoured them with the Torah and with the many prophets among them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وهذا لا ينافي ما يذهب إليه أكثر الأمة من إثبات الشفاعة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والأئمة ع والمؤمنين لأنّ الشفاعة لا تحصل إلا بأمر الله تعالى وإذنه

sources.gloss: This does not conflict with what most of the community holds - that the Prophet, the Imams and the believers intercede - for intercession comes about only by Allah's command and leave.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: اخترناهم على عالمي زمانهم بدلالة قوله لأمة نبينا { كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس }

sources.gloss: We chose them over the world of their own time, as shown by His words to our Prophet's community, 'You are the best nation brought forth for mankind.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: لو كان على ما توهموه انه لا يجر به الى الجزاء في دار أخرى مع ما فيه من الألم لكان لعباً

sources.gloss: were it as they imagine, that it leads to no requital in another abode despite the pain in it, it would be mere play.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: يشفع النبي والأئمة والمؤمنون فى إسقاط كثير من عقاب المؤمنين، لأن الشفاعة لا تحصل إلا بأمر الله واذنه

sources.gloss: the Prophet, the Imams and the believers intercede to lift much of the believers' punishment, for intercession comes about only by Allah's command and leave.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الأئمة من المؤمنين، و فضلناهم على من سواهم

sources.gloss: the Imams from among the believers; and We favoured them over all others.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ما استثنى الله عز ذكره بأحد من أوصياء الأنبياء و لا أتباعهم ما خلا أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام) و شيعته

sources.gloss: Allah made an exception for none of the successors of the prophets or their followers except Amir al-Mu'minin and his shia.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: إلاَّ من رحم الله منهم، فإنه يغني عنه بأن يشفع له عند ربه

sources.gloss: except him on whom Allah has mercy among them, for He avails him by interceding for him before his Lord.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: لا ينفع يومئذ إلا رحمة الله عز وجل بخلقه

sources.gloss: nothing avails on that day except Allah's mercy on His creation.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: نَحْنُ وَالله الَّذِي رَحِمَ الله وَنَحْنُ وَالله الَّذِي اسْتَثْنَى الله لَكِنَّا نُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ

sources.gloss: We, by Allah, are those on whom Allah had mercy; and we, by Allah, are those whom Allah excepted; yet we shall avail them.

essay.en:
This is where the surah closes, and it sets two destinies side by side. It opens on the tree of Zaqqum, the food of the sinful, which boils in the belly like molten copper, seething like boiling water. Al-Mizan reads 'the sinful' as one in whom sin has settled through persistence or excess, and takes the verses that follow as a portrait of the people of the fire [1]. Majma al-Bayan reports that this came down about Abu Jahl, who had mocked the warning by mixing dates and butter and calling it the Zaqqum Muhammad frightens us with [2].

Then the command falls to the keepers of hell: seize him, drag him to the middle of the fire, and pour boiling water over his head [1]. He is told, 'Taste this! Indeed you are the mighty and noble.' Al-Mizan explains that dressing him in might and nobility while he lies in humiliation is mockery meant to sharpen his punishment [1]; al-Tibyan adds that the words throw back at him the very rank he had claimed for himself in the world [4]. This, they are told, is what they used to doubt.

The passage turns. The Godwary stand in a safe place, which al-Mizan glosses as a station secure from every harm [1], amid gardens and springs, dressed in silk and brocade, seated face to face, wedded to houris, calling for every fruit in full security. They taste no death beyond the first they already met, and God guards them from the fire. Al-Tibyan lays out the disputed readings of that exception [5]. All of it is a grace from your Lord, which al-Mizan stresses is pure bounty, owed to no one [1]; that is the great success.

The surah ends as it began, with the Book: We have made it simple in your language so they may take admonition. Al-Mizan calls this the summing-up of the whole surah [1]. So wait; they too are waiting.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi
narrations.arabic: { خذوه فاعتلوه } أي اضغطوه من كل جانب ثم انزلوا به { إلى سواء الجحيم } ثم يصب عليه ذلك الحميم

text.en: 'Seize him and drag him,' that is, squeeze him from every side, then take him down to the middle of hell; then that boiling water is poured over him.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi
narrations.arabic: يقال له { ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم } فلفظه خبر ومعناه حكاية عمن يقول له ذلك وذلك أن أبا جهل كان يقول: أنا العزيز الكريم، فتعير بذلك في النار

text.en: He is told, 'Taste this! Indeed you are the mighty and noble.' Its wording is a statement, but its meaning reports the words of the one who says it to him: Abu Jahl used to say, 'I am the mighty, the noble,' so in the fire he is taunted with it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أيما عبد أقبل قبل ما يحب الله عز و جل أقبل الله قبل ما يحب، و من اعتصم بالله عصمه الله، و من أقبل الله قبله و عصمه لم يبال لو سقطت السماء على الأرض، أو كانت نازلة نزلت على أهل الأرض فشملتهم بلية كان في حزب الله بالتقوى من كل بلية، أليس الله عز و جل يقول: { إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِي مَقَامٍ أَمِينٍ }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Any servant who turns to what God loves, God turns to him; whoever holds fast to God, God protects him. Such a one would not care if the sky fell or a calamity struck the earth's people: by God-wariness he is in God's party, safe. Does God not say, 'Indeed the Godwary will be in a safe place'?

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: لأنْحَلَنَّ لَهُ الْيَوْمَ خَمْسَةَ أَشْيَاءَ مَعَ الْمَزِيدِ لَهُ وَلِمَنْ كَانَ بِمَنْزِلَتِهِ أَلا إِنَّهُمْ شَبَابٌ لا يَهْرَمُونَ وَأَصِحَّاءُ لا يَسْقُمُونَ وَأَغْنِيَاءُ لا يَفْتَقِرُونَ وَفَرِحُونَ لا يَحْزَنُونَ وَأَحْيَاءٌ لا يَمُوتُونَ ثُمَّ تَلا هَذِهِ الآيَةَ لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا الْمَوْتَ إِلا الْمَوْتَةَ الأولى
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Abbas, from al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Sufyan al-Hariri, from his father, from Sad al-Khaffaf, from Abu Jafar

text.en: God said: Today I will grant him five things, and more, for him and for whoever shares his rank. They are youths who never age, sound and never sick, rich and never poor, joyful and never grieved, and living who never die. Then he recited: 'Other than the first death, they will not taste death therein.'

perspectives.en: On who 'the Godwary' are, the two traditions read the word differently. Tafsir al-Qummi glosses them as the Shia of Amir al-Mu'minin, so the promised safety and reward are theirs [10]. Razi, reporting his own school, reads al-muttaqin as broadly as it will stretch: anyone who guarded against idolatry earns the name, so even the sinning believer falls under this promise [32]. The Shia narration narrows the referent to the followers of Ali; the Sunni commentator widens it to every monotheist who kept clear of shirk.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وتوصيفه بالعزة والكرامة على ما هو عليه من الذلة واللأمة استهزاء به تشديداً لعذابه.

sources.gloss: Describing him with might and nobility, in the humiliation and disgrace he is in, is mockery of him, meant to intensify his punishment.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: طعام الأثيم أي الآثم وهو أبو جهل وروي أنّ أبا جهل أتى بتمر وزبد فجمع بينهما وأكل وقال هذا هو الزقوم الذي يخوّفنا محمد به نحن نتزقمه

sources.gloss: 'The food of the sinful,' that is, the sinner, and he is Abu Jahl. It is related that Abu Jahl brought dates and butter, combined them, ate, and said: This is the Zaqqum that Muhammad frightens us with; we gulp it down.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ثم يخاطبه فيقول له { ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم } على وجه التهجين له بما كان يدعي له مما ليس به أي أنت كذلك عند نفسك وقومك

sources.gloss: Then He addresses him: 'Taste! Indeed you are the mighty and noble,' as a way of shaming him with what he used to claim for himself and did not have; that is, you are so in your own eyes and your people's.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقوله { إلا الموتة الأولى } قيل ان (إلا) بمعنى (بعد) كأنه قال بعد الموتة الاولى. وقيل: معنى (إلا) سوى كأنه قال: سوى الموتة الأولى. وقيل: إنها بمعنى (لكن) وتقديره لكن الموتة الأولى قد ذاقوها.

sources.gloss: On 'other than the first death': it is said 'except' means 'after,' as if to say after the first death; it is said it means 'apart from'; and it is said it means 'but,' i.e. the first death they have already tasted.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: { خذوه فاعتلوه } أي اضغطوه من كل جانب ثم انزلوا به { إلى سواء الجحيم } ثم يصب عليه ذلك الحميم

sources.gloss: 'Seize him and drag him,' that is, squeeze him from every side, then take him down 'to the middle of hell'; then that boiling water is poured over him.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وذلك أن أبا جهل كان يقول: أنا العزيز الكريم، فتعير بذلك في النار

sources.gloss: And that is because Abu Jahl used to say, 'I am the mighty, the noble,' so in the fire he is taunted with it.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وصف ما أعده الله للمتقين من شيعة أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام فقال: { إن المتقين في مقام أمين }

sources.gloss: He described what God has prepared for the Godwary from among the Shia of the Commander of the Faithful, saying: 'Indeed the Godwary will be in a safe place.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أيما عبد أقبل قبل ما يحب الله عز و جل أقبل الله قبل ما يحب، و من اعتصم بالله عصمه الله … أليس الله عز و جل يقول: { إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِي مَقَامٍ أَمِينٍ }

sources.gloss: Any servant who turns toward what God loves, God turns toward him, and whoever holds fast to God, God protects him ... Does God not say, 'Indeed the Godwary will be in a safe place'?

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: قال أصحابنا كل من اتقى الشرك فقد صدق عليه اسم المتقي فوجب أن يدخل الفاسق في هذا الوعد

sources.gloss: Our companions said: everyone who guards against idolatry, the name 'the Godwary' truly applies to him, so the sinning believer must be included in this promise.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: لأنْحَلَنَّ لَهُ الْيَوْمَ خَمْسَةَ أَشْيَاءَ مَعَ الْمَزِيدِ لَهُ وَلِمَنْ كَانَ بِمَنْزِلَتِهِ أَلا إِنَّهُمْ شَبَابٌ لا يَهْرَمُونَ وَأَصِحَّاءُ لا يَسْقُمُونَ وَأَغْنِيَاءُ لا يَفْتَقِرُونَ وَفَرِحُونَ لا يَحْزَنُونَ وَأَحْيَاءٌ لا يَمُوتُونَ ثُمَّ تَلا هَذِهِ الآيَةَ لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا الْمَوْتَ إِلا الْمَوْتَةَ الأولى

sources.gloss: I will grant him today five things, and more, for him and for whoever shares his rank: they are youths who never grow old, sound and never sick, rich and never poor, joyful and never grieved, and living who never die. Then he recited: 'Other than the first death, they will not taste death therein.'
